plan.contextChunk: This figure illustrates the architecture of an autoregressive transformer decoder, drawn as a horizontal left-to-right pipeline over a sequence of token positions. At the left, a vertical stack of word-embedding vectors represents the input sequence tokens: <start>, It, takes, great, courage, to, and let. These embeddings enter a large block labeled “Transformer with masked attention,” annotated (× K) to indicate K repeated decoder layers. Inside the transformer block, a lower-triangular masked-attention diagram shows that each token position can attend only to itself and earlier positions, preventing access to future tokens during next-token prediction. The block also shows residual/addition nodes and intermediate feature vectors that pass through the repeated masked-attention layers. At the right, each processed token representation feeds into a “Linear + softmax” block, producing a probability distribution over the vocabulary for the corresponding target token. The target-token labels shown on the far right are It, takes, great, courage, to, let, and yourself, illustrating shifted autoregressive training where the model predicts the next token at each position. This figure introduces the decoder-only transformer architecture for sequence generation, emphasizing causal masking and parallel next-token prediction across positions.

interactionPlan.concept: A decoder-only transformer processes all positions of a prefix in parallel through K repeated masked-attention layers, and causal masking plus a shifted target row make each position predict only the next token.

interactions.label: Decoder layers K
interactions.teaches: The single drawn masked-attention block is shorthand for K identical layers stacked in sequence; raising K expands the (× K) notation into K visible repeated masked-attention + residual stages, showing that depth is repetition of the same causal block

Each stage has a distinct role in next-token prediction: embeddings inject token identity, masked attention mixes only earlier context, residual adds preserve the input signal, and Linear + softmax turns the final representation into a vocabulary distribution

interactions.label: Trace prediction of 'yourself'
interactions.teaches: Following the prefix ending at 'let' through masked attention, the residual adds, and the final Linear + softmax to the bottom output row shows that the 'yourself' distribution is computed using only tokens up to 'let' — the causal mask blocks every later token, which is exactly what makes generation autoregressive

demo_steps.title: The left-to-right pipeline
demo_steps.narration: Input tokens become embeddings, pass through the masked-attention transformer block, and each position's output is mapped by Linear + softmax to a probability row over the vocabulary. Click any block to read its role in next-token prediction.

demo_steps.title: Depth is repeated masking
demo_steps.narration: Drag K upward: the compact (× K) symbol unfolds into K stacked masked-attention + residual stages. Every layer applies the same causal rule, so depth refines representations without ever letting a position see future tokens.

demo_steps.title: Predicting 'yourself'
demo_steps.narration: Collapse back to the compact view and run the trace: the prefix up to 'let' flows through the masked attention and residual adds into the final Linear + softmax, lighting up the bottom probability row labeled 'yourself'. Notice the mask prevents any token after 'let' from contributing.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: Causal masking lets every position be computed in parallel while each one conditions only on earlier tokens — the shifted target row (predicting 'yourself' from the prefix ending at 'let') is what turns that parallel pass into autoregressive generation.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Lay out as a horizontal left-to-right pipeline with four labeled column headers. Left: seven input token labels each pointing to a row of small white embedding boxes inside a dashed 'Word embeddings' container. Center: a large gray dashed rounded rectangle holding an orange lower-triangular masked-attention matrix (connection lines only on and below the diagonal), a circled-plus residual node, a tall teal feature bar, a column of small blue rounded per-token blocks, a second circled-plus, and a second teal bar; place a '(× K)' label with an ellipsis arrow to its right. Right: a column of teal rounded 'Linear + softmax' blocks, each arrowing to a blue probability row (boxes with a dotted ellipsis gap) and a target token label (It, takes, great, courage, to, let, yourself); add small rotated vocabulary labels (a, aardvark, abacus, ..., zero, zeta) under the bottom row. Use orange/brown for the attention matrix, teal for feature vectors and softmax blocks, and steel-blue for embedding and probability boxes. When K increases, vertically stack K copies of the masked-attention + residual motif inside the gray block; the trace animation should highlight the bottom ('let' -> 'yourself') path while dimming later-token contributions to make the causal mask visible.

⚠ Figure failed to load

discrepancies: The transformer block interior is significantly compressed compared to the source: the orange attention matrix is much narrower, and the internal elements (teal bars, blue blocks, ⊕ symbols) are cramped together rather than having the spacious left-to-right flow of the source
The blue feed-forward blocks inside the transformer appear as small oval/circular shapes rather than the clearly rounded-rectangle shapes stacked vertically in the source

The residual skip connections in the source clearly arc over the top of the attention matrix and feed-forward blocks with visible vertical segments; in the generated version they are present but much less prominent due to the compressed layout

The embedding-to-transformer arrow in the source originates from the right edge of the dashed embedding container at the middle row; in the generated version it appears to connect correctly but the embedding boxes are slightly smaller
evaluation.notes: All major components of the GPT decoder pipeline are present with correct labels and colors, and the K-slider and trace animation are pedagogically meaningful, but the transformer block interior is noticeably compressed with wrong proportions for the attention matrix and feed-forward blocks compared to the spacious layout in the source.
action_items: Widen the transformer block and increase internal spacing so the attention matrix, ⊕ symbols, teal bars, and blue feed-forward blocks have proportions matching the source figure's spacious left-to-right flow

Change the blue feed-forward blocks from small oval/circular shapes to clearly rounded rectangles (approximately 18×10px with rx=4) stacked vertically with visible connection lines, matching the source
Make the residual skip connections more prominent with thicker strokes and clearer vertical segments arcing over the top of each sub-block, as in the source

feedback.rationale: The concept, labels, and interactivity are all correct (scores of 4), but the transformer block interior has compressed proportions, wrong shapes for feed-forward blocks, and under-prominent skip connections — all concrete implementation-level fixes that the generator can address without changing the plan.

discrepancies: The attention matrix line pattern in the generated figure creates a denser, more mesh-like visual compared to the source's clean lower-triangular structure with clearly distinct row-to-column connections

The blue rounded-rectangle blocks inside the transformer (representing the feed-forward network) appear noticeably smaller and more compressed in the generated figure compared to the source's clearly distinct, larger rounded rectangles
The source figure has more generous spacing between the transformer block and the Linear+softmax column; the generated version compresses this gap, making the (× K) annotation area feel cramped
evaluation.notes: The generated figure faithfully reproduces all major structural elements of the transformer decoder diagram (embeddings, masked attention matrix, residual connections, teal normalization bars, blue FFN blocks, softmax heads, probability rows, vocabulary labels) with correct colors and topology; the K-slider and trace animation are pedagogically strong additions, though the attention matrix line density and internal block proportions differ slightly from the source's cleaner rendering.
action_items: Reduce the line count or increase spacing in the attention matrix to better match the source's clean lower-triangular visual (currently ~7 lines create a denser mesh than the source's ~5-6 distinct rows)
Increase the size of the blue rounded-rectangle blocks inside the transformer (bbW and bbH) to better match the source's more prominent feed-forward representation
Widen the horizontal gap between the transformer block's right edge and the Linear+softmax column to give the (× K) annotation more breathing room

feedback.rationale: All scores are 4-5 with no failure modes; the discrepancies are minor visual proportion tweaks (line density, block size, spacing) that don't materially affect comprehension or faithfulness — further iteration would yield diminishing returns.
